text: Installing Pollis and Julia, the first launch, and how the Julia packages a panel needs are installed. Pollis is a single application with no account and no licence key. It writes Julia code; Julia, which runs that code, is installed separately, from the Welcome page, in a few minutes.

Download the file for your system from github.com/saragga/pollis/releases/latest. macOS (Apple silicon), Pollis-darwin-arm64.zip: Unzip it and move Pollis.app to Applications. In Terminal, run xattr -cr /Applications/Pollis.app. Open Pollis. Windows (x64), PollisSetup-x64.exe: Double-click it. If SmartScreen warns you, choose More info, then Run anyway. Click Install. No administrator rights are needed. Pollis opens when the installation finishes; later, open it from the Start menu. Linux (x64), Pollis-linux-x64.tar.gz: Run tar -xzf Pollis-linux-x64.tar.gz. Run Pollis-linux-x64/pollis. The apps are not signed yet That is why macOS needs the xattr step and Windows may warn you. Download Pollis only from the link above.

If Julia is not installed, the Welcome page says so under Status: Julia is not installed. Choose Install Julia, then Download and Install. Pollis installs it with juliaup, the official Julia version manager, in a terminal. The terminal says when Juliaup and Julia have been installed. The Welcome page's Status then says Julia found, and the Julia REPL starts. If Julia is already installed somewhere Pollis cannot find it, choose Set Julia Path instead, and give the path of the Julia program in the setting julia.executablePath.

section: The first start of the Julia REPL
text: When Pollis opens, the Julia REPL starts in the panel at the bottom. The first time, it installs DuckDB and PollisDatasets, makes the four built-in databases, PollisDatasets, PollisRSS (empty until feeds are read), PollisJournals and PollisReferences (Built-in Databases, page 40), and says This happens only once. They go into an environment of Pollis's own, ~/.pollis/julia, which comes after yours: your own versions of these packages are used first. At later starts, PollisDatasets, PollisJournals, PollisReferences and PollisRSS are updated from GitHub when there is a newer version; offline, the installed copies are kept.

The Powered by: line at the top of a panel names its Julia packages. Beside it, a tick means they are all installed; Install means some are missing, and installs them in the Julia REPL, in your active Julia environment. You do not have to: the code a panel sends to the Julia REPL or to a notebook starts with a line such as Pollis.packages("GLM", "Plots", "PollisDatasets") which installs whichever of them Julia cannot load, and does nothing when all are there. Replications, notebooks and Code Examples begin the same way. The first run of a panel can therefore take a few minutes; the next ones do not.

Pollis asks GitHub once a day for a newer release. When there is one, a badge appears on the Manage gear, and Download Update opens the file for your system in your browser: install it as above. At the first start of a new version, Pollis offers What's New; Help > What's New in Pollis opens the same notes at any time. To stop the checks, set update.mode to none.

Pollis tells you things in four places, each with its own purpose: Status Whether Pollis is ready: Julia and its version, and the built-in databases, PollisDatasets, PollisRSS, PollisJournals and PollisReferences. Always shown; when something is missing it is a warning with its button. Announcements New releases of Julia, DBInterface, PollisDatasets and PollisTeX, until you dismiss them. Shown only when there is one. RSS The newest unread items of the feeds you follow (page 22); a camera or a microphone marks a video or a podcast, and a journal's items have the tag of its level and metrics. Its Alerts tab shows your alerts and those that fired (page 26). Notifications The bell at the bottom right: what happens while you work, such as new datasets, new content or a toolbox to reload. A faster start If you do not want the Julia REPL at every start, clear julia.startREPLOnStartup. It then starts the first time you send code to it. macOS: ``Pollis is damaged and can't be opened" & Run xattr -cr /Applications/Pollis.app in Terminal, then open Pollis again. Windows: ``Windows protected your PC" & Choose More info, then Run anyway. Julia is not installed, though it is & Choose Set Julia Path and give the path of the Julia program. The first run of a panel seems stuck & Look at the Julia REPL: packages are being installed and compiled. Wait for the prompt to come back. Install stays after installing & The tick appears once Julia has finished; it checks again every few seconds. Not available yet A Mac build for Intel processors, and signed apps.

What a panel is made of, and how to go from its example to code of your own. Each item of the Explore, Model, Simulate and Optimise menus opens a panel: a page about one method, with an example you can run as it is, with simulated data or a dataset from PollisDatasets, and then make your own.

The title, and the Powered by: line: the Julia packages the panel uses, each a link to its documentation, with the tick or Install (see Getting Started, page 2). Key Points: what the method does and when to use it, in a few lines. Decision Table, in some panels: which variant to use for which data. Illustration, in some panels: a picture of the method or its variants. Example Code: the tabs of the panel's variants (above, Bernoulli, Binomial, …), its inputs, and the code. Changing an input changes the code at once. Next Steps and Learn More, at the bottom (next page). Click a section's name to open or close it.

The buttons below the code send it where you want it: Julia REPL runs it in the Julia REPL, starting it if needed. Send to Notebook opens it in a new Jupyter notebook, with the Julia kernel. Send to Pluto opens it in a new Pluto notebook, in Pollis's browser. Send to Editor opens it in a new, unsaved Julia file, and Copy copies it. Code sent to the Julia REPL or to a notebook starts with the line that installs any missing package.

Choose Edit below the code, and change it: your data, your variables, your options. Choose Save, or Cancel to leave it as it was. A saved example is marked Customised, and the panel shows your version from then on. To go back to the original, choose Restore Default, then Confirm Restore within four seconds. Your version goes to the Trash.

section: Add a tab of your own
text: Choose + at the end of the tabs, type a name and press Enter. The new tab, marked Added, opens empty, for editing: write or paste your code, and Save. To remove it, choose the × on the tab, then Delete; it goes to the Trash. Your examples and tabs are files in ~/.pollis/examples, one folder per panel. They are kept when Pollis is updated.

Visualise, Diagnose, Predict, Compare, Interpret: examples that carry on from the Example Code, using its results. Next Steps opens once you have run or sent the Example Code of the tab (the ? beside it says so). Its examples have the same buttons, and can be edited and restored in the same way.

Local Wikis: a reference page on the method, in Pollis. Notebook Tutorials: notebooks that work through the method. Multimedia Tutorials: videos and talks. Add / Edit Video adds your own. Explore References: the papers and books behind the method, with Open in Browser and Copy BibTeX to Clipboard. Add / Edit Reference adds your own, from BibTeX, a link or a DOI; they go into your references, in PollisReferences (page 40), and Edit corrects a work wherever it is cited. The example data are an example They show how the method works. To use it on your own data, change the lines that load the data, and check that the variables and options still suit your question. Next Steps is dimmed & Run or send the Example Code of this tab first. An error that a package is not found & Use Julia REPL or Send to Notebook, which install it, or Install on the Powered by: line. The send buttons are greyed out & Finish editing (Save or Cancel); an added tab needs some code first. Not available yet The microphone and speaker buttons beside the title: voice comes in a later version.

The datasets that come with Pollis, your own databases, and the Databases view. Pollis comes with a collection of real datasets, PollisDatasets, that its examples use, and connects to DuckDB, SQLite and PostgreSQL databases. All the work with data is done in Julia: the Databases view shows what is there and writes the code to reach it.

57 real datasets, such as mroz, airpassengers, iris, and challenger, each with its source and licence. In Julia: datasets() lists them; datasetinfo("mroz") describes one and its columns; data = dataset("mroz") loads one as a Tables.jl table. They are installed the first time the Julia REPL starts (Getting Started, page 2). When new datasets are added, a notification says so.

The same datasets are also a DuckDB database, PollisDatasets, one table per dataset, named after it, with a description of the table and of each column. It is read-only, and is rebuilt only when PollisDatasets changes. The Welcome page's Status says when it is ready. Like the other built-in databases (page 40), it is a DuckDB file, not in the Lance format: Pollis also brings DuckDB's Lance extension, for Lance datasets such as tables of embeddings, but the built-in databases do not need it. Open the Databases view, in the secondary side bar on the right (or choose Open Databases View in the notification of new datasets). Click PollisDatasets, marked built-in. It connects in the Julia REPL as pollis. Expand it to see its tables and their columns. Then query it in the Julia REPL with SQL: DBInterface.execute(pollis, "SELECT * FROM mroz WHERE educ > 12")

Click a connection to connect it in the Julia REPL; Disconnect closes it. On a table, Open in Table Viewer shows its rows; right-click it for Preview Rows in Julia REPL. Show Tables and Hide Tables, beside a connection, expand or collapse it; Refresh Schemas, at the top of the view, shows tables you have just created. Right-click a connection for Copy Name, Copy Connection Code, Edit Connection and Delete Connection, which removes only the saved connection, never the database.

SQL should be at hand wherever you are working, without a second database program: all three use the same DuckDB engine, with the Lance extension, and attach the four built-in databases, read-only. The duckdb> terminal, for SQL alone, without starting Julia: New DuckDB Terminal, at the top of the Databases view (or Databases: New DuckDB Terminal in the Command Palette). It opens an empty database in memory; .help lists its commands, such as .tables, and Ctrl+C stops a long query. The sql> mode of the Julia REPL, for a query in the middle of Julia work: type > on an empty line, then the query, ending in ;. The result is a Tables.jl table in ans, ready for Julia; Backspace on an empty line goes back to julia>. db = PollisDB.connect(), for Julia code and scripts: a DuckDB connection in memory, shown in the Databases view; PollisDB.connect("sales.duckdb") opens a file instead. Lance is loaded in the background, so the connection is ready at once.

In the Databases view, choose New, then DuckDB, PostgreSQL or SQLite. Give a Connection Name and the Julia Variable that will hold the connection, and choose whether to keep it for all your work (Global) or for this folder only (Current Workspace). For DuckDB or SQLite, choose the database file (Choose File). A DuckDB connection with no file is an empty database in memory: it can read CSV and Parquet files in place, and is lost when you disconnect. Read Only protects a file from changes. For PostgreSQL, give the Host, Port, Database and Username. Check the Generated Code, then Save Connection, or Connect to save it and connect. A connection opened by your own code can be shown in the view as well: con = PollisDB.show(DBInterface.connect(DuckDB.DB, "sales.duckdb"); name = "Sales") PostgreSQL passwords With Ask for Password in the REPL (the default), you type the password in the Julia REPL when you connect: it is never written in the code, in the REPL history or in a file. Without it, the password comes from PGPASSWORD or ~/.pgpass.

Explore > Access Files and Databases: SQL Databases (query, import a CSV, Parquet or JSON file, save a table, export a query), CSV Files and Excel Workbooks. Explore > Access Data Libraries: Hugging Face and Kaggle datasets, Yahoo Finance, Alpha Vantage, US SEC EDGAR, FRED and the European Central Bank. A provider that needs an API key shows Set API key on the Powered by: line; the key is kept in your system's secure storage. The view shows no tables & Choose Refresh Schemas. A new database stays empty until you create a table in the Julia REPL. PollisDatasets does not connect & The Julia REPL has not started yet, or is still installing: wait for the Welcome page to say the database is ready. Cannot write to pollis & The built-in database is read-only: save your tables in a database of your own. PostgreSQL does not connect & Check the host, port and SSL Mode; the Connection Timeout is 10 seconds. Not available yet International Monetary Fund Datasets, World Bank Indicators and the Kenneth French Data Library are in Access Data Libraries, greyed out.

Showing only the menus you need, and making Pollis yours. Pollis has hundreds of panels. A View is a named set of the menu items Pollis shows: a course can keep only its own topics, a researcher only their field. The panels you hide are still there; another View shows them again.

The name of the View in use is in the title bar, before the layout buttons: View: Max. Click it for the Views menu, with a tick on the one in use. Two Views are built in: Max shows every menu item. It is the default. Min shows a short selection: the common plots and Descriptive Statistics in Explore, and a few models, simulations and optimisation panels. Switching applies at once, to every menu. The built-in Views cannot be changed or deleted.

section: Make a View of your own
text: In the Views menu, choose Create View..., type its name, and choose the View it starts from: Max starts with every menu item. Or choose Save View As... to copy the View in use. The new View becomes the one in use, and the Views panel opens in the secondary side bar, on the right, after Databases: the menus, with every item below them. Untick an item to hide it, tick it to show it. Unticking a submenu hides everything in it; a submenu shows how many of its items are shown, such as 4/12. Changes apply at once. Explore, Model, Simulate, Optimise, Extend and Compose can be trimmed to the items you tick; in the other menus, such as File or Help, you can hide single items.

Edit View... makes one of your Views the one in use, and shows its items in the Views panel. Delete View... moves its file to the Trash, so it can be restored. Deleting the View in use switches to Max. Open Views Folder opens ~/.pollis/views: each of your Views is a JSON file there. Copy a file to another computer, or give it to your students, to use the same View. The View in use is kept in the setting pollis.view.

Choose the Manage gear at the bottom left, then Settings, and type in the search box a word or a setting's id, such as julia.startREPLOnStartup. Themes > Color Theme, in the same gear, changes the colours, light or dark.

The Extensions pane, in the activity bar on the left, installs extensions from Open VSX, the open registry of extensions, as well as Pollis toolboxes (next topic). Some extensions published only by Microsoft are not on Open VSX, so they cannot be installed in Pollis.

Your own things are files in ~/.pollis, kept when Pollis is updated: views your Views examples your Example Code and added tabs (Inside a Panel, page 4) workflows your copies of the replications (page 14) methods, packages your new methods and their packages (page 16) practice the exercises you write (the Learning and Practice toolbox) rss the items of your RSS feeds (page 22) A hidden item is only hidden A View changes the menus, nothing else: the Command Palette and links between panels still reach every panel. A View is not a way to stop students from opening a panel. A menu item has gone & The View in use hides it: switch to Max, or tick it in your View. The items cannot be ticked & The View in use is built in: choose Save View As... to make an editable copy. An extension is not found & It is not on Open VSX. Look for an open alternative there.

Adding a whole field to Pollis with a toolbox extension. A toolbox is an extension that adds a set of panels to the menus, with their wikis and notebook tutorials. It holds no program code: its panels are made like Pollis's own. Four are published: Financial Econometrics: ARIMAX, VAR and VECM, GARCH-type and regime switching models, forecasting, Bayesian asset-pricing factor models. Economics: business cycle filters, stochastic volatility, DSGE and heterogeneous-agent models, continuous-time macro-finance, game theory. Mathematical Core: symbolic maths, linear algebra, nonlinear systems, numerical differentiation and integration, ordinary and partial differential equations. Learning and Practice: multiple-choice exercises whose data and answers Julia computes, and a panel to write new ones; described in its own guide, Learning and Practice.

Open the Extensions pane, in the activity bar on the left. The Toolboxes section, at the top, lists the toolboxes you have not installed. Click a name for its details. Choose Install. When Pollis asks, choose Reload Now or Restart Extensions. The Toolbox Panels page opens: installing a toolbox does not change your menus until you choose its panels there (next page). An installed toolbox moves to the Installed section. When a newer version is published, it comes back to Toolboxes with Update.

section: Choose its panels, and where they go
text: The Toolbox Panels page shows the toolbox on the left and Your Menus (Preview) on the right. Tick the panels you want (Select All, Select None), or choose Display Author's Suggestion to see where the author would put them. Click a blue line in the preview, Put here, to put the ticked items there. A ticked toolbox menu moves with its panels inside; untick it to move panels out of it. Choose Publish. The page then says In your menus as shown. A toolbox can go in Explore, Model, Simulate, Optimise or their submenus, or in Extend, a menu that appears only when a toolbox puts something in it. To change them later, choose Edit on the toolbox in the Installed section, or Toolbox Panels... in the Command Palette (Compose: Toolbox Panels...). To remove a toolbox, choose Uninstall on it in the same section.

A teacher can package the panels of a course as one toolbox and give it to the students. This is done by your coding agent (Orchestration, page 34), with a skill that writes the toolbox for you. Choose Compose > New Panels and Toolboxes > Package a Toolbox... The agent starts in a terminal. Tell it which panels you want, by their menu titles, the menus they go in and their order, and the toolbox's name and description. It asks for what is missing. It writes a short spec, builds the toolbox and its README, and says where the .vsix file is. To install it, run Extensions: Install from VSIX... in the Command Palette and choose the file. Your students do the same with the file you give them. Then choose its panels, as on the previous page. To change it, edit the spec, raise its version, build again and install the new file over the old one.

Compose > New Panels and Toolboxes > Create a Panel... has your coding agent write a new panel with you. Create Panels from a Request... writes several at once from a request file, which lists the toolbox and, for each panel, its topic, methods and menu. Without a request file open, it opens an example to fill in. New panels can then be packaged as a toolbox. Toolboxes need the Internet to install The list of toolboxes and their files come from GitHub. Once installed, a toolbox works offline. ``Could not load the list of toolboxes" & Check the Internet connection, then choose Retry. Installed, but nothing in the menus & Choose its panels and Publish: Edit on the toolbox, in Installed. The Toolbox Panels page is empty & Reload the window or restart the extensions, as Pollis asked, first. A panel cannot go in a toolbox & Some Pollis panels have code of their own and are marked not portable; the agent says which. Replication, Methods and Workflows Replay a classic. Keep what it teaches. Besides its replication record, a replicated article can leave two things behind: a new method, and a workflow.

It starts from an article, its input data, and either the results it publishes or its authors' code, in any language. If a method the article uses is missing from Julia's packages, it is written first. Then each result is printed beside the published one. Replication, page 14.

A method an article needed and no Julia package had becomes a documented Julia package. Its tests run the article's data and check the published results, within tolerances. It comes with a vignette, and can be published in the Pollis registry. Methods, page 16.

A flat set of procedures, each with its inputs, its outputs and what it runs. Extracted from a replication, it runs on your own data; combined with others, its independent procedures run side by side. Not available yet Replication records (the article, its data, the targets, the Julia code, whether the replication is full or partial, and any differences); Compose > Replication > Replicate a Classical Article...; and Browse Workflows..., Extract a Workflow... and Combine Workflows... in Compose > Workflows.

Replaying a classic paper from its own data, step by step. A replication reproduces a published analysis on its own public data: a Jupyter notebook that follows the article section by section and prints every published value beside Julia's. It shows a method at work on a real question, and that Julia gets the published answer.

Replication Article Panel data: is public capital productive? Munnell (1990) GARCH: volatility after non-trading days Bollerslev and Ghysels (1996) Survival: the Mayo model for primary biliary cirrhosis Dickson et al. (1989) Logistic regression: the Challenger O-rings Dalal, Fowlkes and Hoadley (1989) Threshold autoregression: the lynx and the sunspot cycles Tong and Lim (1980) Dynamic time warping: the UCR archive baselines Dau et al. (2019) Propensity score matching: the NSW experiment and its replications Dehejia and Wahba (1999) Random forests: Breiman (2001) Breiman (2001) LSTNet: long- and short-term patterns in multivariate time series Lai, Chang, Yang and Liu (2018)

Choose Compose > Replication > Browse Replications... The page lists the replications with their article (its DOI, or Web Page when it has none, and Copy BibTeX), the Julia packages and datasets they use, their size, any data they download, and the date they were last updated. Click more under a description to read it all. Click a replication's name. The first time, Pollis makes your own copy in ~/.pollis/workflows, and opens its notebook. Your copy is yours to change: later openings show it as you left it.

Choose the Julia kernel if the notebook asks for one. Run the cells in order, from the top. The first code cell, Pollis.packages(...), installs any package that is missing, so the first run takes longer. Read each section beside the article: the text says which table, figure or page it replicates. The data come from PollisDatasets or from the source the article used. The page says when a replication downloads data, and how much (+ size download); download if asked marks data that it downloads only when you agree.

Most comparisons are small tables: Julia's value in full, the same value rounded as the article prints it, the published value, and the number of decimals they share, or DIFFERENT. Each table's title says where the published value is printed, usually a page or table. Random forests averages 100 random runs, as Breiman did, so it asks instead whether Julia's average and Breiman's differ by less than two standard errors. All the notebooks but the panel-data one end with a section, What differs, and why.

New replications, and new versions of the ones you have, can arrive between releases of Pollis: the page marks them New or Updated until you open them. When your copy is older than the new version, the page says Your copy is older than this version and offers Open Updated Version: the new notebook is saved beside yours, with its date in the name, and your copy is kept. From a replication to a report A replication's notebook can become a LaTeX report or slides: Reports, page 20. The GARCH replication has its own report template. A cell fails: a package is not found & Run the first code cell, Pollis.packages(...), then the others in order. A download fails & Check the Internet connection; the source may be down for a while. Try again later. You changed your copy and want the original & Rename or delete its folder in ~/.pollis/workflows; opening the replication again makes a fresh copy. Not available yet Replicate a Classical Article... is in the menu but not built yet: it says so when chosen. So are Browse Workflows..., Extract a Workflow..., Combine Workflows..., Create Operational Workflow... and Automations..., in Compose > Workflows.

Turning a new method into a tested Julia package, with its vignette. A new method is one no Julia package has yet, taken from an article: its data, the results the article publishes for them, and the code that reproduces them. Pollis makes it a Julia package whose tests are the published values, with a vignette, its documentation, and can publish it in the Pollis registry. Without data and expected results there is no new method.

Choose Compose > Under Construction.... The method's page has five numbered steps, below; its title is at the top: click it to change it. Nothing is saved until you type or add something. Each method is a folder in ~/.pollis/methods.

Article: the Article Link. Pollis opens it in the integrated browser and keeps no copy; Save a Copy... saves one outside Pollis, by default in the data folder of your Pollis Workspace (Reports, page 20). Input Tables, the data the method is computed from: Empty Table to type one in, Add from a Link, Add from PollisDatasets, or Add from Article: give the numbers of the article's tables, such as 3.2, 5.8, and click Ask Agent. Target Tables, the published results the method must reproduce: Empty Table, Add from CSV Files, or Add from Article. Every printed value becomes a test of the package. A table typed in by the agent keeps every value as printed, and the agent lists the values it could not read for certain: check them against the article. The tests are only as right as the targets.

Write Instructions for the agent, saved in INSTRUCTIONS.md: what the method does, where it is in the article, what to watch for. Then click Write Method: your coding agent writes the code in src, with you, and runs the tests. Edit method.toml shows the method's own file: its tables, its call and its article. Open Code opens the code.
Once the method's tests pass, write notes on the vignette (VIGNETTE.md) and click Write Vignette: the agent writes it in LaTeX, with its PDF. Edit Vignette and Open PDF open them.

Give the Package Name: a capital letter, then letters and digits, such as ThresholdAR; the Pollis registry asks for at least 5 characters. It also asks for a usage example and a docstring for every exported name: Prepare for Registration has the agent check the method and fix what it can.

Each button runs in a terminal. Package and Test makes the package in ~/.pollis/packages, runs its tests and checks the registry rules. Package, Test and Push to GitHub then pushes it to its own public repository, if its tests all pass. Package, Test, Push and Register then registers it, if it meets the rules. Pushing needs a GitHub Owner, a user or organization, and the GitHub CLI, gh, signed in; Pollis asks first: Push to GitHub as …?

Compose > Methods > Browse Methods lists yours, In Progress and Published by You, then the Library of nine methods by Pollis, from arc-fs to threshold autoregression: click one to open your own copy. Delete and Delete Empty Methods move folders to the Trash. Help > Documentation > Package Vignettes lists the vignettes of installed packages (they open offline) and, with the Internet, those In the Registry. The agent steps cost tokens Add from Article, Write Method, Write Vignette and Prepare for Registration run your coding agent, on your account. …has no target tables, so nothing to test & Add the published results in Target Tables. Copies are kept outside Pollis & Save the copy outside ~/.pollis, e.g. in a Pollis Workspace. The push fails & Sign in with gh auth login in a terminal, and check the GitHub Owner.

The Julia packages written for Pollis, which you can also use without it. Most panels use Julia packages from Julia's General registry. Fourteen packages are Pollis's own: nine methods, and five packages behind panels and features. All are public on GitHub, under Trumpingtons, with the MIT licence, and work in any Julia session, with or without Pollis. None is in the General registry.

The nine methods of the Library in Compose > Methods > Browse Methods (Methods, page 16). Each is tested against the published results of the article it comes from, has a vignette, and is in the Pollis registry. Package Topic Tested against ArcFS Boosting Breiman's arc-fs, from his random forests article BreslowCox Survival analysis The Mayo model of primary biliary cirrhosis ErrorComponents Panel econometrics Baltagi's tables for the Grunfeld, gasoline and public capital data ForestOOB Random forests Breiman's out-of-bag errors and variable importance GLMExtras GLM inference Dalal, Fowlkes and Hoadley's Challenger O-ring analysis LSTNet Time series forecasting Lai, Chang, Yang and Liu's LSTNet-Skip and their PyTorch code PeriodicGARCH Volatility Bollerslev and Ghysels's periodic GARCH PropensityMatching K-nearest neighbours Dehejia and Wahba, and its replications ThresholdAR Nonlinear dynamics Tong and Lim's threshold autoregression

Add the Pollis registry once, then add packages by name, in the Julia REPL's package mode (type ]): pkg> registry add https://github.com/Trumpingtons/PollisRegistry pkg> add ThresholdAR Help > Documentation > Package Vignettes opens the vignettes of the packages you installed.

Package What it does Where Pollis uses it PollisDatasets small, well-known datasets for examples and teaching, as Tables.jl column tables The built-in database (Data and Databases, page 6), Add from PollisDatasets in Methods, and the examples of panels and replications PollisTeX Typesets LaTeX from Julia with Tectonic, downloaded on first use Compose > Reports (Reports, page 20) EDGAR Fetches SEC EDGAR filings and financial data Explore > Access Data Libraries > US SEC EDGAR HARE Heteroskedasticity and autocorrelation estimators Model > Linear Models: Linear Models with Heteroskedasticity, with Autocorrelation and with Heteroskedasticity + AR(1) RangeVol Range-based volatility estimators The Range-Based Volatility Estimation panel, not in the menus at present

Pollis installs these packages by itself when a panel, a replication or a report needs them. To install one yourself, give its GitHub address, in the Julia REPL: import Pkg; Pkg.add(url = "https://github.com/Trumpingtons/HARE.jl") The datasets' own terms The MIT licence covers PollisDatasets' code. Each dataset keeps the terms of its provider: datasetinfo("penguins") shows its description, the source to cite, its licence and its columns. add ThresholdAR: the package is not found & Add the Pollis registry first, as above. Pkg.add("HARE"): the package is not found & These five are in no registry: install with Pkg.add(url = ...), as above.

From a notebook to a LaTeX report or slides. Any Jupyter notebook, a replication's or your own, can become a LaTeX report (an article) or beamer slides, with its outputs and figures and a PDF beside it. Pollis does this in its Julia REPL, without an agent; a coding agent can then polish the draft into a finished document.

section: Before you start: a Pollis Workspace
text: Reports are written in the reports folder of a Pollis Workspace: an ordinary folder for your own work, outside Pollis. To make one, choose File > New Pollis Workspace..., then choose or create a folder, for example in your Documents, and click Make Pollis Workspace. Pollis puts a pollis.toml file and a data folder in it, and opens it. Next time, open that folder with File > Open Folder....

Open the notebook, for example your copy of a replication (page 14). Choose Compose > Reports > Export Notebook as LaTeX... for a report, or Make Slides from a Notebook... for slides. The notebook's own toolbar has the same two in its Export button: LaTeX Report... and Beamer Slides.... With no notebook open, Pollis asks you to choose one, starting in ~/.pollis/workflows. The Julia REPL installs PollisTeX if it is missing, runs the notebook's code cells in order and compiles the document. The .tex opens in the editor, and the PDF beside it, in the integrated browser. The files are in reports/NAME of the workspace, NAME being the notebook's: report.tex or slides.tex and its PDF, each cell's printed output in outputs/cellN.txt, and its figure in figures/cellN.pdf.

A report is a draft of the notebook's text cells, with the printed outputs and figures in their place and without the code. Slides have a frame for the text under each heading, and one for each output and each figure. A notebook with a template, a latex folder beside it, gets that document instead, with its own tables, figures and references. The GARCH replication ships one for its report.

Edit the .tex as you like, then click Compile LaTeX, the play button at the top right of its editor: Pollis saves it, compiles it with PollisTeX in the Julia REPL and reloads the PDF. Exporting the notebook again refreshes the outputs and figures, and keeps your .tex: Pollis writes it only when the folder has none. To start the draft again, delete the .tex first.

Open the report's or the slides' .tex. Choose Compose > Reports > Polish with Agent... The coding agent starts in a terminal in the report's folder. It turns the draft into a finished document: sections, tables, captions and citations, from the numbers already computed. It does not run the notebook again, and it compiles the document as it goes: the PDF beside you reloads each time. Polish runs on the Light tier of Model Routing (Orchestration, page 34). Polish costs tokens The menu item with the sparkle runs your coding agent, on your account. Read the result: an agent can still misplace a value, so check the numbers against the draft. Reports are written in the reports folder of a Pollis Workspace & Click New Pollis Workspace..., or open your workspace folder. A Pollis Workspace keeps your work outside Pollis & Choose a folder outside ~/.pollis, for example in your Documents. No PDF appears & A cell or the compile failed: read the error in the Julia REPL, fix it, and export or compile again. Polish says to open the .tex & Open report.tex or slides.tex first, then choose Polish with Agent... again.

Following news, journals, central banks, searches, podcasts and videos, and keeping what they bring. Explore > RSS > RSS Feeds opens a page with the feeds you follow on the left, by topic, and their items on the right. Pollis reads every feed when it starts and then every hour; Refresh reads them at once. The feeds are read by your computer, not by a server of Pollis. At first, Pollis follows only the Julia news; a notification at the first launch points to the catalogue, where you choose the rest. Every feed is RSS to Pollis, wherever it comes from: most come from the catalogue, about 520 feeds in 35 categories, from PollisRSS.jl and updated without a new Pollis, ranging from Classics and Philosophy to Economics and Astronomy, all listed on the page in alphabetical order; some are searches you save, at arXiv or PubMed; and some are email alerts, saved searches whose results arrive by email, which Pollis turns into feeds. They are read, shown, archived and added to Zotero alike.

Explore > RSS > Add Feed..., or Add Feed on the RSS Feeds page, opens a page with these sections: From an Address a feed's address, the page of a journal or a website, or a YouTube channel or its @handle; Find From a Search a PubMed or arXiv search, such as abs:"survival analysis" AND cat:stat.ME; Preview first From Email Alerts the alerts mailbox, and the alerts that arrived in it, ticked to follow (below) Your Feeds the feeds you added, with Remove; under Removed Feeds, Restore For a journal's page at Wiley, Taylor & Francis, SAGE, Elsevier, Cambridge Core or Oxford Academic, Find gets the feed of its newest issues; for another website, the feeds its page lists, to choose from when there are several. Then pick the topic to list the feed under, or New Topic....

Click a topic or a feed on the left to see its items, or All Feeds. The feeds of a topic are indented under it, with a camera after the name of a feed of videos and a microphone after a podcast's. Every topic of the catalogue is listed; one with no feed subscribed starts collapsed. The last column, Unread / Total, counts the items of the Items From period. The items are shown 100 at a time, newest first; Previous and Next, above and under them, turn the pages. Click an item to open it in your browser; it is then marked read, and its title is no longer bold. Mark Unread, shown when the pointer is on a read item, marks it unread again. An item of a podcast or a video has a Listen or Watch link; Pollis tells them by the feed, or by the item's address (a news site's video or audio page). Three columns of circles, for a feed or for all the feeds of a topic: green when on, red when off, half green and half red when only some of a topic's feeds are on; the last two are under Display. Subscribed: Pollis reads the feed every hour, and a catalogue feed ticked is followed (its count is a dash until then); unticked, it is no longer read, but its items stay. Here: its items are shown on this page; unticked, they are hidden here and on the welcome page, but the feed is still read and archived, and the right says No items shown when every item of a choice is hidden. Welcome Page: its newest unread items are in the welcome page's RSS section. Items From sets how far back items are shown: The Last 7 Days, 30 (the default), 90, or All Items Kept. Items without a date are always shown. On a Day... shows the items of one day, chosen in a calendar. Only the latest items of each feed are kept here, and the archive goes back only to the day you started following it: a feed cannot tell what happened before then. An item of a journal has a purple tag: the journal's level in the Norwegian register (Level 2 leading, Level 1 academic, Level 0 not academic), OpenAlex's 2-year mean citedness (Cited 7.9), and, once you have imported them (Built-in Databases, page 40), the SJR or Impact Factor quartile and its year (SJR Q1 2025). The pointer on the tag shows every value known, with its source and year: SJR and its categories, SNIP, IPP, h-index, open access. Pollis knows the journal of a catalogue feed, of an email alert's article, and of a feed you added, by looking up its first items once. Journals, next to Items From, shows only the items of some journals: Academic (Level 1 or 2), Leading (Level 2), Open Access, and, once imported, SJR Q1, SJR Q1–Q2 and SNIP Above 1. Items not from a journal (news, blogs, preprints) always stay, and the counts follow the choice. Remove, shown when the pointer is on a feed, takes it off the page; Restore, under Removed Feeds on the Add Feed page, brings it back.

Explore > RSS > Journal Metrics, More Metrics... in Journals, the i next to it, or a click on a tag opens the Journal Metrics page: each source's metrics, their values and meaning, and more to import (page 40).

Add to Zotero, shown when the pointer is on an item, adds it to Zotero 7 or later, open on the same computer: an article from PubMed as a journal article, an arXiv, medRxiv or bioRxiv paper as a preprint, a video or a podcast episode as such, and anything else as a web page. When Zotero has collections, Pollis asks which one, starting from the last one you chose. The item then shows In Zotero, and is listed in the zotero view of PollisRSS (below), with the collection. For an open-access paper, an arXiv, bioRxiv or medRxiv preprint or a PLOS article, Zotero also downloads its PDF and attaches it. For any other article, use Zotero's own Find Available PDF (right-click the item in Zotero), which finds a free copy when there is one. Export as OPML saves the feeds you follow as one file, to follow them in Zotero (File > New Feed > From OPML...) or another feed reader. PubMed searches and email alerts are left out, since only Pollis reads them.

Every item Pollis reads is added to a monthly file in ~/.pollis/rss/items, so an item stays when its feed drops it. PollisRSS is a DuckDB database over those files, made with PollisDatasets the first time the Julia REPL starts (Data and Databases, page 6), and empty until feeds are read: In the Databases view, click PollisRSS, marked built-in. It connects in the Julia REPL as rss, read-only. Query its four views: items, one row per item (feed, topic, title, link, published, received, summary, picture and media); feeds, one row per feed with its number of items; zotero, the items added to Zotero; and episodes, the podcast episodes downloaded. DBInterface.execute(rss, "SELECT topic, count(*) FROM items GROUP BY topic")

An item of a podcast has Download Episode, which saves its audio file in ~/.pollis/rss/episodes, a folder per podcast; the notification's Open Folder shows it, and the item then shows Downloaded. The episode is listed in the episodes view of PollisRSS, with the file. Videos are not downloaded, since YouTube's terms do not allow it, and news pages stay links.

Google Scholar, JSTOR, HeinOnline, Nexis Uni, SSRN, Semantic Scholar, Web of Science, Scopus, Westlaw and Factiva send the results of a saved search only by email. Send them to an address of your own, best one used only for alerts, and Pollis turns each alert into a feed, with the title, the link, and the authors and journal of each result. Pollis reads the mailbox on your computer over IMAP, read only: nothing passes through a server. Add Feed, From Email Alerts: the address, its IMAP server (suggested for Gmail, iCloud, Yahoo, Fastmail and GMX) and its password, kept in the system's keychain; then Connect. Gmail, iCloud and Yahoo need an app password; Outlook.com does not let programs in with a password. Create the alerts at each source, sent to that address. The Email Alerts skill, in Compose > Agent Skills, walks you through each source and writes precise searches in its syntax, so the alerts bring few false hits. Alerts in the Mailbox lists the alerts that have arrived, by source; the ones you tick are listed under the topic Email Alerts. Google Alerts (Show options > Deliver to > RSS feed) and the table-of-contents alerts of many publishers are feeds already: paste their address in From an Address; Search Feeds from Other Services there shows where EBSCOhost and ProQuest give theirs. Alerts on quotes, SEC filings and economic data Warnings when a quote crosses a level, a company files at the SEC or a series publishes a new value are not feeds: Alerts, page 26. Press releases from PR Newswire, and what the news said around an event: Media Coverage, page 24. Could not be read the last time; the items shown are the ones read before & The feed's site did not answer, or moved: try Refresh later, or remove the feed and add its new address. No feed found at this address & On the journal's page, look for an RSS link and copy its address; for an Oxford journal, the RSS icon on its page. The mailbox could not be read & Check the address, the server and the password; Gmail, iCloud and Yahoo need an app password, and IMAP turned on. Zotero is not open & Open Zotero 7 or later on this computer, and click Add to Zotero again. The episode could not be downloaded & The podcast's site did not answer: check the internet connection and click Download Episode again. A YouTube channel shows no videos & YouTube's feeds are sometimes unavailable for a while: the items come at a later reading.

What the news said about a company, an institution or a subject, and when. Explore > Media Coverage counts the articles about a company, an institution or a subject over a period, by hour, day or week, marks the FOMC's releases, a company's SEC filings or a time of your own on the same chart, and lists the articles, newest first. Pollis shows the headlines and links only; an article opens in the internal browser.

Words: what the articles must have. Quotes keep a phrase together ("Apple Inc"); OR between words takes any of them, in parentheses: (iPhone OR iPad). Words can be a subject, such as "going concern", or an institution: "FOMC" OR "Federal Reserve". Sources: tick the ones to search; Pollis keeps your choice. Yahoo Finance has a Ticker box beside it (AAPL): its headlines, and the company's SEC filings for Mark. Period: Last 24 Hours, Last 3 Days, Last 7 Days, Last 30 Days, Last 90 Days, Last Year, or From a Day to a Day, with a From and a To day of your own. Mark: Nothing, FOMC Releases, SEC Filings of the Ticker or A Time, of your own; then Search.

Google News papers and sites the world over, among them those with no search of their own, such as The Washington Post and The Times; at most 100 articles a search Yahoo Finance the latest headlines of the ticker: the newest only, not the whole period The New York Times its Article Search, with your own free key: the newest 50 articles of the period The Guardian its Open Platform, with your own free key: the newest 1,000 articles of the period PR Newswire companies' and organisations' own press releases; unticked at first

section: The keys of The New York Times and The Guardian
text: Both give a free key for personal use. Beside each, Get a Free Key opens its sign-up page in the internal browser; Set Key... asks for the key, kept in the system's keychain, never in a file. Change Key... replaces it; left empty, the key is forgotten. A source ticked without a key says No key set and is skipped; the others are still searched.

Coverage gives the number of articles from each source, listed of those it found, and a chart of them by hour, for up to 3 days, by day, for up to half a year, or by week. A mark is a dashed line where it falls. Click a bar to list only its articles, and Show the Whole Period to list them all again. Articles lists each with When, From (the outlet), Headline and Source. The same story told twice, by an outlet and its copy elsewhere, is listed once.

A paid distribution service: companies and organisations pay it to put out their own press releases, unedited. Most are corporate (results, deals, dividends, products), but they come from every sector, from health to technology to entertainment, often before the 8-K that EDGAR shows, and with their time to the second. Its feeds list only the latest releases, so Pollis reads them every 10 minutes while PR Newswire is ticked here, or while there is an event study of SEC filings, and keeps them on this computer. A search finds only the releases out since then: those that have all its words, or give the ticker as the wires do, such as (NASDAQ: AAPL). From an event study Each event of an event study has a News link (Event Studies, page 28): it opens Media Coverage from the day before the event to the day after, with the event marked. For an FOMC release, the words are "FOMC" OR "Federal Reserve"; for a filing, the company's name, with its ticker. The other wires GlobeNewswire and Business Wire keep programs away from their feeds, and Pollis respects that: their releases, and ACCESS Newswire's, come through Google News, with the time it gives, which can be later than the release. What it does not do Google News lists at most about 100 articles a search: over a long period, or for a company much in the news, it leaves gaps, and a shorter period, or more precise Words, finds more. FOMC releases go back about a year, as far as the Federal Reserve's feed. Pollis counts articles; it does not read them or judge their tone. No key set: The New York Times & Get a Free Key, then Set Key... beside it, or untick it. Not reached: Google News & Check the internet connection and Search again; the articles of the other sources are still shown. Nothing found & Fewer or broader words, without quotes, or a longer period. Search stays grey & Tick a source, and give Words or a Ticker, and a whole period. No PR Newswire releases & Only the releases out since it was ticked are kept: search a later period.

Being told when a quote or an economic series does something unusual, or when a company files something new at the SEC. An alert watches one thing for you while Pollis is open: a quote at Yahoo Finance, looked up every minute; a company's filings at the SEC's EDGAR, looked at every 15 minutes; or an economic series at FRED, the ECB, the IMF or the World Bank, looked up every hour. When it fires, a notification stays until you act on it, in the colour you chose, and the status bar shows how many fired alerts you have not read. Nothing runs on a server: when Pollis is closed, nothing is watched.

Explore > Alerts > Add Alert..., with Alert On set to A Quote. Symbol: an index (^GSPC), a share (AAPL), a future (BZ=F) or a currency (EURUSD=X); Look Up shows its latest value and a chart over 1 Day, 5 Days, 1 Month or 6 Months. Alert Me When It: Crosses Above or Crosses Below a value; Is Above or Is Below it, once until it is back on the other side; or Moves By more than a percentage since the previous close. The value is drawn across the chart. Or one of the statistical conditions below. Shows As Information, Warning or Error; Fires Every Time the condition is met anew, or Once, after which the alert is paused. Then Add Alert. The quotes are delayed by up to about 20 minutes, depending on the exchange.

Add Alert..., with Alert On set to Economic Data, and From: FRED, ECB, IMF or World Bank. FRED asks for a free API key, set once with Set FRED Key and shared with the FRED panel. Series: a FRED series ID (CPIAUCSL, UNRATE); an ECB dataset and key (EXR/D.USD.EUR.SP00.A); an IMF dataflow and key; or a country and a World Bank indicator (PRT/NY.GDP.PCAP.KD). Look Up shows its title, latest value and period, frequency, units and a chart. Alert Me When It Publishes a New Value; crosses, or is above or below, a value; Changes By at least an amount from the value before; or a statistical condition. The first look only notes the latest period; from then on, each new period is checked. A revision of a period already published does not fire. Open Series opens the series at its source.

For a quote or a series, an alert can fire on what is unusual for it, rather than on a value you choose. OnlineStats.jl computes these in Julia, in a hidden process that Pollis starts when needed; the first time, it installs OnlineStats and JSON3 in an environment of its own, ~/.pollis/alerts/julia, which takes about half a minute. Your own environments are not touched. A quote's move is from one minute to the next, as a log return; a series' move is its change from the value before. Moves Unusually: a move larger than so many Standard Deviations of the moves before it. Leaves Its Band: the value leaves the band of so many standard deviations around its mean; once, until it is back within. Moves Beyond a Quantile: a move beyond that quantile, in per cent, of the moves before it; above 50 a rise, below 50 a fall. Makes a New High or Low: above the highest or below the lowest of so many Values Before It. The mean and the standard deviation weigh recent values more: Half-Life, in Values is after how many a value weighs half as much. The chart then shows what the alert would have done: its band over each minute of the last five days' regular sessions, or over the series' latest values, with a dot where it would have fired, and how many times. Change the numbers until it fires as rarely as you want. Open Notebook beside the count opens alert.ipynb, which computes the same with OnlineStats.jl over the same values, to check it or try other settings; your changes to it are kept.

EDGAR is where companies listed in the United States publish their reports: the annual 10-K, the quarterly 10-Q, and the 8-K for events that cannot wait, such as results, a merger or a new chief executive. Explore > Alerts > Add Alert..., with Alert On set to SEC Filings. The first time, Set Contact: your name and email, which the SEC asks for with every request. It is kept in your system's keychain and shared with the US SEC EDGAR panel; it is sent only to the SEC. For: One Company, Several Companies, An Industry or Every Company, the last only with Contains, as there are thousands of filings a day. Company: a ticker (AAPL) or the SEC's CIK (320193); Look Up lists its recent filings, those of the chosen forms and items in bold. Companies: tickers or CIKs separated by commas. Industry: an SIC code, such as 2834 for pharmaceuticals (SIC Codes opens the SEC's list); every company the SEC files under it, listed or not. Forms: separated by commas, 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K at first. An amendment (10-K/A) counts as its form; left empty, every filing fires. 8-K Items, when the forms take in 8-Ks: an 8-K then fires only when it reports one of the items ticked, such as 2.02 Results of Operations, 5.02 Directors or Officers Changed or 4.02, a restatement; none ticked, every 8-K fires. Contains, optional: words the filing must have, in EDGAR's full-text search; an exact phrase in quotes, such as "going concern". Search lists the filings of the last 30 days that have it, each opening the document, so you see how often the alert would fire. Then Add Alert. The first look only notes the company's latest filing. From then on, each new filing of those forms fires, the oldest first; with Once, only the first. The notification's Open Filing opens the document at the SEC in your browser, and the alert keeps the second EDGAR accepted the filing. Without Contains, several companies and industries are looked for in EDGAR's latest filings, which go back about a day: filings made while Pollis is closed for longer are missed. With it, the full-text search goes back as far as needed, though it may index a filing some minutes after it is published.

In Explore > Access Data Libraries, Yahoo Finance and Alpha Vantage have Alert Me... beside their Symbol, US SEC EDGAR beside its CIK, FRED, ECB and IMF beside each tab's Series, and World Bank on its One Indicator tab: it opens Add Alert with the symbol, company or series filled in.

Explore > Alerts lists Your Alerts, each with its latest value and period or latest filing, and Pause, Resume and Remove; a quote opens its Quote page, with your alerts drawn across the chart, and a filing alert opens the company's page at EDGAR. Fired Alerts lists what fired, with the value before and after, the band it left for a statistical condition, or the filing and Open Filing; Mark Read and Mark All Read clear them. The welcome page has an Alerts tab beside RSS with the same. Alerts are kept in ~/.pollis/alerts/alerts.json (Open alerts.json), and fired alerts in history.jsonl beside it. With several windows open, only one of them looks things up. Event studies The filings an alert fires can be the events of a study of how the stock moved around them: Start Event Study on the alert, or Auto Event Study when you add it (Event Studies, page 28). Yahoo Finance does not know …, or could not be reached & Check the symbol at Yahoo Finance's site, as it is written there (^GSPC, BZ=F), and the internet connection. The SEC does not know …, or could not be reached & Try the CIK instead of the ticker: some filers have no ticker in the SEC's list. Check the internet connection. Needs your SEC contact & Set Contact on the Add Alert page, under SEC Filings: a name and an email address. Needs your FRED key & Set FRED Key on the Add Alert page, under Economic Data. Needs Julia & A statistical condition is computed in Julia: install it (Install Julia, page 2), and the alert goes on. Julia is installing OnlineStats.jl & The first time only; the alert is checked again within the minute. An alert fired late & Quotes are delayed by up to about 20 minutes, filings are looked at every 15 minutes and series every hour; nothing is looked up while Pollis is closed.

How stocks move around SEC filings, and rates, yields and stocks around the FOMC's releases, a minute at a time; and how an outcome moves when units are treated at different times. An event study measures how something moves around events. A market event study follows prices in the minutes around them: the SEC filings an alert fires, with the minute prices of each filer's stock and of a benchmark; or the FOMC's releases, with federal funds and SOFR futures, Treasury yields, TIPS and the S&P 500. While Pollis is open it captures the prices from Yahoo Finance as they come and draws the result on the page. A panel event study follows an outcome over the years, quarters or months after units are treated at different times: states adopting a policy, firms a rule, or the clinics of a stepped-wedge trial crossing from control to treatment one group after another, from a table of your own. Either way the study is a folder that a notebook analyses with PollisEventStudies.jl.

An alert on SEC filings chooses the events: its companies, forms, 8-K items and words (Alerts, page 26). Add Alert... on the page makes one. Compose > Workflows > Event Studies..., New Study: a Title, Kind Market Event Study, Events SEC Filings, and the alert. Benchmark: a Yahoo Finance symbol, ^GSPC for the S&P 500 at first. Normal Return: Market-Adjusted takes the benchmark's return out; Market Model takes out alpha plus beta times it, estimated on the minute returns of the regular sessions of the Estimation Days before the period. Event Time: First Public, the earlier of the company's newswire release and EDGAR's acceptance, as results are often on the wires hours before the 8-K; or EDGAR Acceptance alone. Periods: minutes Before and After the event, at first 30 and 120; Next Open also follows an event outside the regular session from the next open. Add Period adds another. Then Make Study. A new study starts with the filings the alert would have fired in the last 30 days, as Yahoo Finance keeps minute prices for 30 days, and adds each filing the alert fires from then on. On the alert, Start Event Study opens this page with the alert chosen, and Auto Event Study starts a study with the settings above the first time the alert fires.

For each filing, Pollis looks for the company's release on GlobeNewswire, Business Wire, PR Newswire or ACCESS Newswire from a day before EDGAR accepted it to a day after: in Google News, and in PR Newswire's own feeds, which Pollis reads every 10 minutes while there is a study of filings and which give the time to the second (Media Coverage, page 24). The events show the Release, the Accepted time and the Lead of one over the other; News opens Media Coverage around the event.

New Study, Market Event Study, FOMC Releases: which releases are events (the statement, the Summary of Economic Projections, the minutes, other), and the Instruments, by what their move tells: Target Rate Surprise (FF1, the current month's federal funds future), Path and Forward Guidance (FF2 to FF4, SOFR futures, the 2-year note future ZT) and Fed Information Effect (^FVX, ^TNX, TIP, ^GSPC, ES). The period is 10 Min Before, 20 After, the tight window of Gürkaynak, Sack and Swanson (2005). A new study starts with the releases of the last 59 days, with five-minute prices for those older than 30 days.

Your Studies lists each study, with its events and how many are still capturing prices. Open one: A study of filings draws the cumulative average abnormal return (CAAR), in per cent, with its 95% band, and each event's in grey, From the Event or From the Next Open; under it, the articles about the events. Events lists each filing: Company, Form, When (during the session, before the open or after the close), Prices and its CAR. A study of FOMC releases draws each instrument's average move from the start of the period, with its 95% band, in basis points for rates and yields and in per cent for prices, and lists the releases. Open Folder, Edit study.toml and Open Notebook.

Each study is a folder in ~/.pollis/event-studies: study.toml, its settings; events.csv, the events with their times in UTC; prices/, a file of bars per event; and, for filings, news/, the articles about each. Open Notebook opens study.ipynb, which installs PollisEventStudies.jl from the Pollis registry and runs it on the folder: filings: for each period, the average and cumulative average abnormal returns a minute at a time with their t, the CAR's t, the Boehmer, Musumeci and Poulsen (1991) test, and abnormal volume; FOMC releases: each instrument's move at each release, the mean move with its t, and the mean move a minute at a time. The results are written to results/. Events still capturing prices count up to the last complete minute: run the notebook again as they come in. What it does not do Prices are captured only while Pollis is open; a study catches up on reopening within Yahoo Finance's 30 days of minute prices (60 of five-minute prices), and an event older than that has none. A filer without a ticker has no prices. An expired futures contract is gone from Yahoo Finance, so FF1 of a past month has none, and Yahoo Finance has no 2-year yield in minutes: ZT stands for it, as a price. No alert on SEC filings yet & Add Alert... on the page, with Alert On set to SEC Filings. No prices at Yahoo Finance & The stock did not trade around the event, or Yahoo Finance does not list it. Older than the 30 days of minute prices & The event came before what Yahoo Finance keeps: it stays in the events, without prices. Some are not among the events & The last 30 days had more filings than EDGAR's full-text search reads: narrow the alert.

A panel study is made from a table of your own rather than from prices Pollis captures, and nothing happens until its notebook runs. New Study: a Title and Kind Panel Event Study. Table, Choose File...: a CSV file with a row per unit and time (or per individual, unit and time). Its columns and first rows are shown, and it is copied into the study's folder as panel.csv. Times are whole numbers: years, or quarters or months numbered in order. Columns: the Unit (also the clusters of the standard errors), the Time and the Outcome. Treated: a Treatment Indicator, not 0 from the time a unit is treated, or a First Treated column, the time each unit is first treated, missing or 0 for never. Choose each one: what a column means cannot be read from its name, and a column called treat may only say which units are ever treated. Estimators, one or more: Two-Way Fixed Effects and Sun and Abraham: the regression on leads and lags of the first treatment with unit and time effects, and Sun and Abraham's (2021) estimator, which stays right when the effects differ between cohorts; Callaway and Sant'Anna: their (2021) effect of each cohort at each time, against the Control units (Never Treated, Not Yet Treated, Treated Last, or Auto, the never treated when there are any), by a Method (Doubly Robust, Inverse Probability Weighting, Outcome Regression), and its averages; Stepped Wedge: the mixed model of Hussey and Hughes (2007) for a trial whose clusters cross to treatment one group after another, with an Effect (Immediate Treatment, one effect; Exposure Time Indicators, one for each time since the cross; or Heterogeneity by Exposure Time), averaged over exposure times From to To or taken At one, and an Outcome Type, continuous or binary (0 or 1, or successes out of Trials). It needs a treatment indicator. Event Times: the Leads before the first treatment, for the test of pre-trends, and the Lags after it. Then Make Study.

Your Studies shows the table, its columns and the estimators. Open Notebook opens study.ipynb, which installs PollisEventStudies.jl from the Pollis registry (and MixedModels.jl for the stepped wedge), runs the estimators study.toml names on panel.csv and writes the results to results/. The page then draws: each estimator's effects by event time with their 95% intervals, 0 being the first time treated (the stepped wedge's exposure time 1), and a table of them; the tests of pre-trends: an F test of the effects before treatment; Callaway and Sant'Anna's averages: simple, over event times, over cohorts and over calendar times; the stepped wedge's estimate, with the intracluster correlation. The page redraws when results/ changes: after an edit of study.toml, run the notebook again. Which estimator Two-way fixed effects averages the effects with weights that can be negative when the effects grow over time, because units treated earlier serve as controls for those treated later. Sun and Abraham, and Callaway and Sant'Anna, compare each cohort only with units not yet or never treated; when they agree with each other and not with two-way fixed effects, trust them. Units treated from the first time have no time before treatment to compare with, and the estimators leave them out. No results yet & A panel study: open its notebook and run it. Pre-trends: not tested & Callaway and Sant'Anna's test takes every cohort's effect at every time before treatment; with more of them than units, as with many cohorts over many years, it cannot be made. Their effects by event time before 0 still show any pre-trend. Not a table & The file needs a header row and three columns or more, separated by commas. The stepped wedge needs a treatment indicator & Under Treated, choose Treatment Indicator and a column that is not 0 from the time a unit is treated.

Working with others at their own computers: a chat, and sharing code, datasets, files and databases. A session connects up to five people, each at their own copy of Pollis: two colleagues, a student and a tutor, or a small team. Everyone keeps their own editors and notebooks; in the chat you talk, and you share what you choose, when you choose. Nobody can change anything on anyone else's computer.

Pollis on each computer, and an Internet connection. A network that lets sessions through. To check, choose Compose > Collaboration > Test Connection... before the session, and send its results (Copy Results) if you need help.

Choose Compose > Collaboration > Start Side by Side Session... Type your name, as the others will see it. The chat opens beside your editor, and the invitation is copied to the clipboard. Paste the invitation into an email or a message to the others. To copy it again, use Copy Invitation at the top of the chat, or Compose > Collaboration > Invite People... You are the host: you admit the others, up to five in all, and when you leave the session ends for everyone.

Choose Compose > Collaboration > Join Session... Paste the invitation you received, or type its code: four groups of five letters and digits, such as 7KQ2M-.... Type your name. The chat opens and says when you have joined.

Write a message and press Enter; Shift+Enter starts a new line. Paste or drag an image into the message: larger images are reduced to fit the limit of 2 MB. The + button in the message box adds: Image: a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP image, shown in the chat. File: any file up to 5 MB. The others get a card with Save As...; Pollis never opens or runs it. Dragging a file that is not an image into the chat shares it the same way. Dataset: a CSV file up to 5 MB (see the next page). Database: a DuckDB database up to 5 MB (see the next page). Show Participants lists who is in the session and whether each connection is direct or through a relay. The invitation is the key Anyone with the invitation can join while the session lasts, and receives whatever is shared from then on. Send it only to the people you mean, and do not share personal or confidential data in a session whose invitation may have gone further.

While you are in a session, a bar at the bottom of each editor and notebook shows Share My Editor. It sends a snapshot of what you see, unsaved changes included; a notebook is sent without its outputs. For a Pluto notebook in Pollis's browser, use the Share My Editor button in the browser's toolbar. Sharing again replaces the earlier snapshot. Code files and notebooks up to 2 MB can be shared. The others see your snapshot read-only, with two buttons below it: Compare with Mine: your snapshot and their own editor side by side, line by line. Copy to My Editor: replaces the content of their own editor, or the cells of their own notebook, with yours. Undo brings theirs back, except in Pluto.

A dataset (CSV): + > Dataset in the chat, Share Dataset on a CSV file in the Explorer, or Share Dataset in the toolbar of a Julia table viewer. Pollis asks before sending. The others get a card with the first five rows and Preview, Save to My Workspace and Load into My Julia Session, which reads it into a Julia table named after the file. A database (DuckDB): + > Database. Pollis asks before sending the whole database. The others get a card with Save As... and Attach in My Julia Session, which opens it read-only, as a variable named after the file, and shows its tables in the Databases view. Before sharing a database Changes made in a Julia session that still has the database open may not be in the file yet: close that connection, or run CHECKPOINT, before sharing. And attach only databases from people you trust: a database can hold views that read files on the computer where they are queried.

Leave Session, at the top of the chat or in Compose > Collaboration, leaves the session. When the host leaves, the session ends for everyone. If the host's connection drops, the others wait a minute for it to come back. After the session the chat stays open, to be read, until you close it.

Free public servers introduce the participants to each other; after that each pair connects directly. The servers never see the session code or anything you share. By default they are nostr relays; on networks that block those, set pollis.collaboration.signalling to mqtt before starting the session (the invitation tells the others). A relay for networks that block direct connections is not set up yet. ``Could not reach the session" & Check the code, and that the host is still in the session. Then run Test Connection... on both computers. Test Connection: no introduction server reachable & The network blocks Pollis (often a firewall or proxy): try another network, such as a phone's hotspot. Test Connection: nostr blocked, MQTT reachable & The host sets pollis.collaboration.signalling to mqtt and starts a new session. Two people never connect & Both networks may block direct connections, which need the relay that is not set up yet: one of them tries another network. ``The session is full" & A session has at most five participants, the host included. A file, dataset or database is refused & It is over 5 MB, or not what it says it is: send it the usual way. Not available yet Start Same Page Session... (editing together), Invite an Agent..., Session Settings..., Classroom and Simulation Games are in the menu but not built yet: they say so when chosen.

Choosing and starting coding agents, and routing tasks to models. Some tasks of the Compose menu are done by a coding agent, a program that writes code and documents in a terminal: creating panels, packaging toolboxes, writing methods and vignettes, polishing reports. Their menu items carry a sparkle, because they run on your agent's account and cost tokens. Pollis works with any agent: you choose which, and which model each task runs on.

Choose Compose > Coding Agents. The page lists Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode, each with its command and whether it is On This Computer: Agent Installed, or Install Agent, which opens its install page. Click Use beside yours; it then shows In Use. Click Install Skills, so that the agent knows the Pollis skills in any folder, even outside Pollis. Later, Update installs their latest version. Each agent also has a local command, under Local and Cloud Models, that runs it on a model on this computer through Ollama or LM Studio: free and private. For any Other Agent, type its command line with {prompt} where the first message goes; without it, Pollis copies the message to the clipboard, to paste into the agent. The choice is kept in pollis.agents.command.

section: What happens when a task starts
text: Pollis opens a terminal, starts the agent there and gives it a first message that points it to the skill for the task. From then on you talk to the agent in that terminal.

A skill is the know-how an agent reads to do a task. Compose > Agent Skills lists them, downloaded in their latest version when the page opens: create-panel, package-toolbox, prepare-method, references, write-method and write-vignette, each with its Tasks and Example Requests. View Skill opens it; Run with My Agent starts your agent on it.

Not every task needs the strongest model. Compose > Orchestration > Model Routing has three tiers: Light: small tasks, on a fast, cheap or local model. Standard: everyday tasks. Strong: hard tasks, where a mistake costs most. Give each tier the command line of an agent, with {prompt}, such as claude --model haiku {prompt} for Light. An empty tier runs your main agent, and so does a tier whose program is not installed. Each task runs on a tier by default: Task Menu Tier Polish with Agent Reports Light Write a Vignette, Prepare for Registration Methods Standard Package a Toolbox New Panels and Toolboxes Standard Tables from the Article, Write a Method Methods Strong Create a Panel, Create Panels from a Request New Panels and Toolboxes Strong In Tasks, choose another tier for a task, or Main Agent. The settings are pollis.agents.tiers and pollis.agents.taskTiers.

Compose > Local Models has Hugging Face Models and Kaggle Models, to find models, and Local Model Runners. A local model runs only through a runner, a program that loads it and serves it on this computer: Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp or Apple MLX. The page shows which are installed, and how each agent reaches each one. An agent works on your files A coding agent reads and writes files, and runs commands, in its terminal. Read what it proposes, and check its results, as you would a colleague's. Choose the coding agent Pollis starts & Choose one in Compose > Coding Agents, then the task again. The coding agent … was not found & Install it (Open Install Page), or choose another one. … tier: … isn't installed & The task ran on the main agent: install the tier's program, or change its command. Not available yet Writer and Checker..., Two Independent Transcriptions... and Race... are in Orchestration but not built yet.

Finding the articles that matter on a topic, bringing in references of your own, and following citations from a few works you know. Literature Radar asks two free, open indexes of scholarly works, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar, and keeps what you choose in PollisReferences (Built-in Databases, page 40). It has four pages: Discover Literature..., Import References..., Browse References... and the Snowball Search Map.

Under Indexes, tick OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar or both. Each lists its 200 most cited articles; with both, the two lists are merged into one. Type a Topic, and choose Search In (Title and Abstract, or Title), a Field, the Years, Citations At Least and Recent Citations In the Last N Years. To keep only the best, choose an Influence percentile, a Journal Ranking (2-year mean citedness, the Norwegian levels, or SJR quartiles once imported), or Only Articles Anyone Can Read. Click Search. The table shows the citations Since Publishing and in the Last N Years, Influential citations, FWCI and Percentile; versions of one article are shown once, with +N versions. Click a title for its Abstract. Tick articles, then act on them: Save to PollisReferences, Copy BibTeX, Open PDFs, Show in Panel..., See in References, or Snowball Search..., which makes them the seeds of a map. Reconcile Sources asks each index for the counts of the articles only the other found. Keys are optional and free Without a key, OpenAlex gives everyone on your network about 100 searches a day between them, and Semantic Scholar asks searches to wait at busy times. A key of your own has its own budget or rate. Click Get a Free Key, then Set Key...; Pollis keeps it in the system's keychain.

Bring references you already have: Paste them, or choose Files and Choose Files.... BibTeX, BibLaTeX, RIS, CSL-JSON and lists of DOIs are read; the format is told by the text itself. Tick Look Up in OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar for their citation counts and the fields your file lacks (by DOI, else by title), then Import. The Tick links (All, None, Found, Not Found, Not Looked Up, Not Yet Saved) choose what Look Up Ticked, Remove Unticked... and Save to PollisReferences work on.

Browse References... lists everything in PollisReferences: the works Pollis cites, those you saved and those you imported, with the same actions. It is where a Snowball Search Map finds its seeds when you type in Add Seeds.
From a few works you know, follow the works citing them, a step at a time, until the steps bring little new. The map has two pages of its own (Snowball Search Map, page 38).

Discover Literature lists the most cited, which favours older work. Sort by Last N Years or FWCI (citations against works of the same field and year) for recent work that already stands out, and use Percentile to compare fields. Influential counts the citations Semantic Scholar finds weighed on the work, not only mentioned. The free budget of OpenAlex … is used up for today & Try again tomorrow, or set a free key of your own. OpenAlex could not be reached, or refused the search & Check the connection, and try again. Semantic Scholar could not be reached, or is too busy just now & Search again a little later, with OpenAlex alone, or with a key. … has no record of this work & The other index may have it: look up its DOI there. Not found in OpenAlex (Import) & Its title or first author differs from OpenAlex's: correct the file, or keep it as it is.

Following citations from a few works you know, a step at a time, and telling when to stop. A keyword search finds what uses your words. A snowball search finds what a literature actually builds on: start from a few works you know are central, the seeds, list the works citing them, make the best of those seeds in turn, and go on. Works cited by several seeds rise to the top, whatever words they use. Pollis follows citations forward, to the works citing each seed, and backward, to the works each seed cites, from OpenAlex.

A dashed box is where seeds came from: Discover Literature, or PollisReferences for those found in Add Seeds. A pill is a seed, filled when chosen: E1 Jia (2019) is the first seed, by Jia, of 2019. Seeds are numbered E1, E2… in the order they were added. A box with ≡ is a list: L1 120 is the first list, the 120 works OpenAlex has citing E1 (up to the 2,000 most cited).
